name: Xiao-Feng-San (Chinese herbal formula)
short: Small or low-quality trials only. Severe eczema (47 given it): no side effects reported (some found it unpalatable). Urticaria: fewer adverse reactions with a modified form than with antihistamines.
text: Safety data on Xiao-Feng-San come only from small or low-quality trials, and the cited abstracts do not describe what kinds of adverse events occurred. In an 8-week randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in 71 patients with severe, treatment-resistant atopic dermatitis (47 given oral Xiao-Feng-San), patients reported no side effects, although some commented on the unpalatability of the medicine; 56 patients completed treatment and follow-up. A meta-analysis of 11 randomised trials in 1076 patients with chronic urticaria found a lower rate of adverse reactions with modified Xiaofeng powder (the abstract does not describe how the formula was modified) than with antihistamines (odds ratio 0.23), but the authors rated the quality of the included research as relatively low and said the findings need confirming in high-quality studies. In a randomised trial in 156 adults with non-severe atopic dermatitis, all of whom took Xiao-Feng-San decoction for four weeks alongside real or sham ear acupuncture, adverse events were mild and transient; the trial had no comparison group that did not take the formula. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
